arxiv-1902-01956.title: Simultaneous Acoustic Trapping and Imaging of Microbubbles at Clinically Relevant Flow Rates
arxiv-1902-01956.creator: Sevan Harput, Luzhen Nie, David M. J. Cowell, Thomas Carpenter, Ben Raiton, James McLaughlan, and Steven Freear
arxiv-1902-01956.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Sevan Harput, Luzhen Nie, David M. J. Cowell, Thomas Carpenter, Ben Raiton, James McLaughlan, and Steven Freear. Mechanisms for non-invasive target drug delivery using microbubbles and ultrasound have attracted growing interest. Microbubbles can be loaded with a therapeutic payload and tracked via ultrasound imaging to selectively release their payload at ultrasound-targeted locations. In this study, an ultrasonic trapping method is proposed for simultaneously imaging and controlling the location of microbubbles in flow by using acoustic radiation force.

arxiv-2008-03255.title: Optimal quantization for discrete distributions
arxiv-2008-03255.creator: 1 Russel Cabasag, 2 Samir Huq, 3 Eric Mendoza, 4 Mrinal Kanti Roychowdhury
arxiv-2008-03255.description: Abstract . In this paper, we first determine the optimal sets of n n -means and the n n th quantization errors for all 1 ≤ n ≤ 6 1\leq n\leq 6 for two nonuniform discrete distributions with support the set { 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 } \{1,2,3,4,5,6\} .

arxiv-2103-16181.title: On the elasticity of polymer model networks containing finite loops
arxiv-2103-16181.creator: Michael Lang
arxiv-2103-16181.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Michael Lang. Based upon the resistor analogy and using the ideal loop gas approximation (ILGA) it is shown that only pending loops reduce the modulus of an otherwise perfect network made of monodisperse strands and junctions of identical functionality. Thus, the cycle rank of the network with pending structures removed (cyclic and branched) is sufficient to characterize modulus, if the resistor analogy can be employed.

arxiv-2104-02190.title: Normal stability of slow manifolds in nearly-periodic Hamiltonian systems
arxiv-2104-02190.creator: J. W. Burby, E. Hirvijoki
arxiv-2104-02190.description: Abstract M. Kruskal showed that each nearly-periodic dynamical system admits a formal U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) symmetry, generated by the so-called roto-rate. We prove that such systems also admit nearly-invariant manifolds of each order, near which rapid oscillations are suppressed.

arxiv-2106-05900.title: Classical algorithms and quantum limitations for maximum cut on high-girth graphs
arxiv-2106-05900.creator: ID Boaz Barak, ID Kunal Marwaha
arxiv-2106-05900.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by ID Boaz Barak, ID Kunal Marwaha. We study the performance of local quantum algorithms such as the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for the maximum cut problem, and their relationship to that of classical algorithms.

arxiv-2112-10480.title: Coincident-point rigidity in normed planes Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. 52C25, 05C10, 52B40, 46B20 Key words and phrases: bar-joint framework, global rigidity, non-Euclidean framework, count matroid, recursive construction, normed spaces, analytic norm
arxiv-2112-10480.creator: Sean Dewar, John Hewetson, Anthony Nixon
arxiv-2112-10480.description: Abstract . A bar-joint framework ( G , p ) (G,p) is the combination of a graph G G and a map p p assigning positions, in some space, to the vertices of G G . The framework is rigid if every edge-length-preserving continuous motion of the vertices arises from an isometry of the space.

arxiv-2203-12098.title: Learning by non-interfering feedback chemical signaling in physical networks
arxiv-2203-12098.creator: Vidyesh Rao Anisetti, 1 B. Scellier, 2 J. M. Schwarz 1,3
arxiv-2203-12098.description: Abstract Both non-neural and neural biological systems can learn. So rather than focusing on purely brain-like learning, efforts are underway to study learning in physical systems. Such efforts include equilibrium propagation (EP) and coupled learning (CL), which require storage of two different states—the free state and the perturbed state—during the learning process to retain information about gradients.

arxiv-2211-00319.title: Random tangled currents for φ 4 \varphi^{4} : translation invariant Gibbs measures and continuity of the phase transition Institut Camille Jordan (Lyon 1), panis@math.univ-lyon1.fr , severo@math.univ-lyon1.fr
arxiv-2211-00319.creator: Trishen S. Gunaratnam, Christoforos Panagiotis
arxiv-2211-00319.description: Abstract We prove that the set of automorphism invariant Gibbs measures for the φ 4 \varphi^{4} model on graphs of polynomial growth has at most two extremal measures at all values of β \beta . We also give a sufficient condition to ensure that the set of all Gibbs measures is a singleton.

arxiv-2301-11250.title: Lattice models for ballistic aggregation: cluster-shape dependent exponents
arxiv-2301-11250.creator: Fahad Puthalath, Apurba Biswas, V. V. Prasad, R. Rajesh
arxiv-2301-11250.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fahad Puthalath, Apurba Biswas, V. V. Prasad, R. Rajesh. We study ballistic aggregation on a two dimensional square lattice, where particles move ballistically in between momentum and mass conserving coalescing collisions. Three models are studied based on the shapes of the aggregates: in the first the aggregates remain point particles, in the second they retain the fractal shape at the time of collision, and in the third they assume a spherical shape.

arxiv-2306-15613.title: Incommensurate Magnetic Order in the ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} Kagome Metal GdV 6 Sn 6
arxiv-2306-15613.creator: Zach Porter, Ganesh Pokharel, Jong-Woo Kim, Phillip J. Ryan, Stephen D. Wilson
arxiv-2306-15613.description: Abstract We characterize the magnetic ground state of the topological kagome metal GdV 6 Sn 6 via resonant X-ray diffraction. Previous magnetoentropic studies of GdV 6 Sn 6 suggested the presence of a modulated magnetic order distinct from the ferromagnetism that is easily polarized by the application of a magnetic field.

arxiv-2407-10322.title: Building Collaborative Learning: Exploring Social Annotation in Introductory Programming
arxiv-2407-10322.creator: Francisco Gomes de Oliveira Neto, Felix Dobslaw
arxiv-2407-10322.description: Abstract . The increasing demand for software engineering education presents learning challenges in courses due to the diverse range of topics that require practical applications, such as programming or software design, all of which are supported by group work and interaction. Social Annotation (SA) is an approach to teaching that can enhance collaborative learning among students.

arxiv-2504-04163.title: Representations of p p -adic groups and orbits with smooth closure in a variety of Langlands parameters Thanks: Clifton Cunningham’s research is supported by NSERC Discovery Grant RGPIN-2020-05220. Thanks: Andrew Fiori thanks and acknowledges the University of Lethbridge for their financial support
arxiv-2504-04163.creator: Kristaps Balodis, Clifton Cunningham, Andrew Fiori, Qing Zhang
arxiv-2504-04163.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kristaps Balodis, Clifton Cunningham, Andrew Fiori, Qing Zhang. In this paper we prove the forward direction of the conjecture of Gross-Prasad that an L-packet Π ϕ ​ ( G ) \Pi_{\phi}(G) contains a generic representation if and only if L ⁡ ( s , ϕ , Ad ) L(s,\phi,\Ad) is regular at s = 1 s=1 , by assuming the local Langlands correspondence and the p p -adic Kazhdan-Lusztig hypothesis.

arxiv-2505-09068.title: S-DAT: A Multilingual, GenAI-Driven Framework for Automated Divergent Thinking Assessment
arxiv-2505-09068.creator: Jennifer Haase, Paul H. P. Hanel, Sebastian Pokutta
arxiv-2505-09068.description: Abstract This paper introduces S-DAT (Synthetic-Divergent Association Task), a scalable, multilingual framework for automated assessment of divergent thinking (DT)—a core component of human creativity. Traditional creativity assessments are often labor-intensive, language-specific, and reliant on subjective human ratings, limiting their scalability and cross-cultural applicability.

arxiv-2510-01017.title: Malliavin differentiability of McKean-Vlasov SDEs with common noise
arxiv-2510-01017.creator: Jianhai Bao, Gonçalo dos Reis, Zac Wilde
arxiv-2510-01017.description: Abstract We establish the Malliavin differentiability of McKean-Vlasov stochastic differential equations (MV-SDEs) with common noise under the global Lipschitz assumption in the space variable and the measure variable. Our result gives also meaning to the Malliavin derivative of the conditional law with respect to the common noise.

arxiv-2510-09480.title: What is the contribution of gravitational infall on the mass assembly of star-forming clouds? A case study in a numerical simulation of the interstellar medium. ∗ noe.brucy [at] ens-lyon.fr
arxiv-2510-09480.creator: Noé Brucy ∗ 1,2, Enrique Vázquez-Semadeni 3, Tine Colman 1, Jérémy Fensch 1, Ralf S. Klessen 2,4
arxiv-2510-09480.description: Abstract Star formation in galaxies is a complex phenomenon occurring on a very wide range of scales, and molecular clouds are at the heart of this process. The formation of these structures and the subsequent collapse of the gas within them to form new stars remain unresolved scientific questions.

arxiv-2512-11577.title: Context-Dependent Effects and Concurrency in Guarded Interaction Trees DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Journal: TOPLAS CCS: Theory of computation Logic and verification CCS: Theory of computation Program semantics
arxiv-2512-11577.creator: Sergei Stepanenko, Emma Nardino, Virgil Marionneau, Dan Frumin, Amin Timany, Lars Birkedal
arxiv-2512-11577.description: Abstract . Guarded Interaction Trees are a structure and a fully formalized framework for representing higher-order computations with higher-order effects in Rocq. We present an extension of Guarded Interaction Trees to support formal reasoning about context-dependent effects. That is, effects whose behaviors depend on the evaluation context, e.g. , call/cc , shift and reset .

olalla.title: Olalla
olalla.creator: Robert Louis Stevenson
olalla.description: Stevenson's Spanish tale of atavism and a decaying noble line — degeneration horror anticipating the century's anxieties about blood. Extracted complete from The Merry Men.

plos-pone-0009213.title: In Situ Hybridization Analysis of the Expression of Futsch , Tau , and MESK2 Homologues in the Brain of the European Honeybee ( Apis mellifera L.)
plos-pone-0009213.creator: Kumi Kaneko, Sayaka Hori, Mai M. Morimoto et al.
plos-pone-0009213.description: PLOS ONE research article. The importance of visual sense in Hymenopteran social behavior is suggested by the existence of a Hymenopteran insect-specific neural circuit related to visual processing and the fact that worker honeybee brain changes morphologically according to its foraging experience. To anal

pmc-10680582.title: Effect of controlled hypotensive hemorrhage on plasma sodium levels in anesthetized pigs: An exploratory study
pmc-10680582.creator: Rafael T Krmar, Stephanie Franzén, Leif Karlsson, Helin Strandberg, Susanna Törnroth‐Horsefield, Jesper K Andresen, Boye L Jensen, Mattias Carlström, Robert Frithiof
pmc-10680582.description: Perioperative hyponatremia, due to non‐osmotic release of the antidiuretic hormone arginine vasopressin, is a serious electrolyte disorder observed in connection with many types of surgery. Since blood loss during surgery contributes to the pathogenesis of hyponatremia, we explored the effect of bleeding on plasma sodium using a controlled hypotensive hemorrhage pig model.

pmc-11392806.title: Spindle architecture constrains karyotype evolution
pmc-11392806.creator: Jana Helsen, Md Hashim Reza, Ricardo Carvalho, Gavin Sherlock, Gautam Dey
pmc-11392806.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The eukaryotic cell division machinery must rapidly and reproducibly duplicate and partition the cell’s chromosomes in a carefully coordinated process. However, chromosome numbers vary dramatically between genomes, even on short evolutionary timescales. We sought to understand how the mitotic machinery senses and responds to karyotypic changes by using a series of budding yeast strains in which the native chromosomes have been successively fused.

pmc-11688352.title: Influence of vaccination against infectious diseases on the carbon footprint of fattening pigs: a systematic review
pmc-11688352.creator: Julia Gickel, Clara Berenike Hartung, Amr Abd El-Wahab, Julia Hankel, Christian Visscher
pmc-11688352.description: IntroductionIn all sectors of the economy, including livestock production, there is an increasing focus on sustainability criteria. The carbon footprint is therefore an important target value in pig production. The aim is to minimize this value. Infectious diseases may affect the performance negatively, potentially leading to a higher carbon footprint.

pmc-11715380.title: Sex/Gender Differences in the Pattern of Comorbid Depressive Symptoms, Pain, and Sleep Problems among Older Mexican Americans With and Without Probable Dementia
pmc-11715380.creator: Sadaf Arefi Milani, Trinity Brigham, Yong‐ Fang Kuo, Brian Downer, Kyriakos S. Markides, Mukaila A Raji
pmc-11715380.description: BackgroundDepression, pain, and sleep problems commonly co‐occur (overlap) among older adults. Data are lacking on the extent, pattern and sex/gender differences of overlap of these symptoms in adults aged ≥80 and living with dementia. Our objective was to examine patterns and sex/gender differences in overlapping depression‐pain‐sleep symptoms among older Mexican Americans with and without probable dementia.

pmc-12427619.title: Sex Disparities in Cardiogenic Shock: Risk Factors, Treatment Intensity, and Mortality in a Single Latin American Country
pmc-12427619.creator: Alexandra Arias-Mendoza, Héctor González-Pacheco, Amada Álvarez-Sangabriel, Diego Araiza-Garaygordobil, Pamela Ramírez-Rangel, Rodrigo Gopar-Nieto, Maria del Carmen López-Rodríguez, Daniel Sierra-Lara-Martínez, Salvador Mendoza-García, Braiana Ángeles Díaz-Herrera, María Nila Papaqui-Quitl, Jaime He
pmc-12427619.description: Background:Cardiogenic shock (CS) carries a high in-hospital mortality, with limited data on sex-related disparities in Latin America. Women remain underrepresented in CS studies.Objectives:To evaluate sex-specific differences in characteristics, management, and mortality in acute myocardial infarction–related (AMI-CS) and non-AMI-CS in a large Latin-American cohort.

pmc-12606090.title: Minimal clinical predictors enable machine learning detection of hepatocellular carcinoma in a Filipino cohort
pmc-12606090.creator: Ranzivelle Marianne L. Roxas-Villanueva, Mojhune Gabriel Manzanillo, Edhel S. Tripon, Dannah Zemirah G. Junio, Marc Daniel O. Jamindang, Ramonito B. Nuique, Beatrice J. Tiangco, Jason R. Albia, Christian M. Alis
pmc-12606090.description: Despite significant advancements in the diagnosis and treatment of Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the overall prognosis remains challenging due to its multifactorial nature. Recently, machine learning has been increasingly utilized in HCC-related research, offering significant advancements in diagnostic accuracy and early detection. However, the application of these techniques in diverse populations, particularly underrepresented groups, remains limited.

pmc-12711570.title: Integrated genomic analysis and CRISPRi implicates EGFR in Alzheimer’s disease risk
pmc-12711570.creator: Yuk Yee Leung, Pavel P. Kuksa, Luke Carter, Jeffrey Cifello, Emily Greenfest-Allen, Otto Valladares, Louisa Boateng, Shannon Laub, Natalia Tulina, Sofia Moura, Aura Ramirez, Katrina Celis, Fulai Jin, Ru Feng, Gao Wang, Phil De Jager, Jeffery M. Vance, Liyong Wang, Struan F. A. Grant, Gerard D. Schel
pmc-12711570.description: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous loci linked to late-onset Alzheimer’s disease (LOAD), but the pan-brain regional effects of these loci remain largely uncharacterized. To address this, we systematically analyzed all LOAD-associated regions reported by Bellenguez et al. using the FILER functional genomics catalog across 174 datasets, including enhancers, transcription factors, and quantitative trait loci.

pmc-12719664.title: Leaflet-specific effects of charged lipids on a voltage-gated potassium channel
pmc-12719664.creator: Takahisa Maki, Masako Takashima, Masayuki Iwamoto, Shigetoshi Oiki
pmc-12719664.description: Voltage-gated potassium (Kv) channels possess distinct voltage-sensor (VSD) and pore (PD) domains, making it challenging to study domain-specific lipid effects. Here, we examined the functional modification of a prototypical Kv channel, KvAP, by phosphatidylglycerol (POPG) and phosphatidylserine (POPS) in mono-component asymmetric bilayers using the contact bubble bilayer (CBB) method.

pmc-12749939.title: Age-related evolution of human gingiva towards a fibrotic-like connective phenotype
pmc-12749939.creator: Chiara Cecchin-Albertoni, Olivier Deny, Laetitia Pieruccioni, Marielle Ousset, Pilar Oreja-Fuentes, Emmanuelle Arnaud, Christophe Guissard, Louis Casteilla, Valérie Planat-Bénard, Philippe Kémoun, Paul Monsarrat
pmc-12749939.description: Periodontal disease affects most adults over 50, but the role of aging in periodontal homeostasis remains poorly understood. This study examines variations in human gingival gene expression over time using transcriptomic and histological approaches. Results show a global decline in gene expression with age, suggesting a loss of genetic information that could weaken the gingiva’s ability to respond to stressors.

pmc-13079059.title: Antimicrobial evaluation of Cardiospermum halicacabum L. leaf fractions and its usage in active bioactive film formation for shelf-life enhancement in fresh-cut fruits
pmc-13079059.creator: Uma Venkatesan, Rajiniraja Muniyan
pmc-13079059.description: Food wrapping plays a critical role in maintaining the superior quality, protection, and preservation of food commodities by preventing contamination and spoilage. The current study investigated the biological potential, chromatographic profiling, molecular docking, and simulation studies of Cardiospermum halicacabum L. leaf fractions. pmc-13254078.title: Association between creative self-efficacy and innovation literacy among undergraduate nursing students: a correlation analysis
pmc-13254078.creator: Ruiqi Lyu, Zhenhong Zhou, Yaliqin Wang, Mengya Xu, Ni Zhang, Fenglin Xu, Jiaxin Wang, Ziang Chu, Hongdan Li, Jianghua Wu
pmc-13254078.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundHealthcare professionals frequently encounter unanticipated workplace challenges, positioning innovation literacy as an essential competency for career advancement. As future practitioners, undergraduate nursing students require adequate innovation literacy to support the optimization of clinical nursing practice and nursing education.
